tasks.short: Prepare reports that document patients' care activities.

steps.what: Ask the ward nurses what care the patients received.
Read those patients' care notes on the patient record.
Mark on the patient record which activities reports document.
Place each selected activity row from the patient record into the reports.
Draft the reports in the patient record from marked notes.

loop.input: The report shell from s4, the activity selection from s3, and the phrases she marked in s2. No medicine code and no unselected row.
loop.output: Draft sentences of the care-activity report.
loop.check: Every sentence names only an activity the selection already lists, and points at a phrase in the marked notes or the short result on that activity row. It adds no activity, diagnosis, medicine or dose.
loop.stop: One pass. If any sentence fails the check, or she marked no note, the draft stays blank and she writes the report.
loop.why_not_simpler: The care notes are free text. A fixed template cannot phrase what the note said, and a rule cannot tell a supported sentence from a line the note does not state.

steps.what: Check the reports in the patient record cite the notes.
File the confirmed reports on the patient record.

tasks.design: The specialist still asks the ward, reads the notes, and marks which activities the reports document. {OTHER}, the electronic patient record, places only those selected activity rows into the shell, and a bounded loop phrases only those rows and the notes she marked, staying blank if a line adds an activity. She checks that text before {OTHER} files it, and no microphone is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Care activities were already on the record, then typed again into a report.
tasks.enabler_now: The record can place the rows she selected, and a bounded loop can phrase only those rows and the notes she marked.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing which activities matter, and a period whose rows were never entered.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which care mattered for these patients and whether a note is complete enough to document.

ambition.what: Every patient in the period she chose gets a confirmed care-activity report the same week, including short stays that used to stay unwritten.

tasks.altitude: She still asks the ward, reads the notes, and chooses the activities. Confirmed reports keep that choice. Filing no longer means typing the same text twice.

reach.task: Enter the care activity when it is given
reach.learn: Enter the activity code at the time of care. A row with no code is left out of the report.
Keep the confirmed report, not the draft, for the dossier period.

evidence.claim: A care-activity report states what was done for the patient during a period, using notes and activity entries already on the record.
Autoscriber records the consultation, the clinician validates, and the note can be stored in the patient record.
Across 236,153 generated notes in one European health system, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes.
The patient dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.
Providers must know whether a generative tool is a medical device, assess risks, train, test and monitor it.
Solely automated decisions that significantly affect a person need a stated basis.
Ambient recording that captures staff performance needs works-council consent.

assumptions: Activity-row contract, used by s4 and not created in this task: patient id, activity code, activity time, performing role, short result. Producer is the nurse who gave the care, entered on the electronic patient record when the care was given. That entry is another task. Its time is not saved here. A row with no activity code is left out of the shell. If the period has no coded rows, the shell stays empty and she writes the report.

She marks the note phrases in s2 and the activity selection in s3. Both stay at remaining 100. The loop may use only those phrases and the selected rows. If she marked no note, the narrative stays blank.
If the patient record already lists activity rows for a period, s4 uses that list. No second store is built.
Filing in s7 stores only the confirmed text from s6. A blank draft means she writes the report and the filing step does not run. The report is not a prescription.
No ambient microphone, so the ward conversation is not recorded. Works-council consultation still applies to edit logs on care notes. The study minutes on generated notes are not this task's saving.

Where the digest names Dutch rules, the dossier retention period applies. Elsewhere, national rules apply. One hour per 100 baseline hours is a monthly sample of filed reports for a line the notes do not support.
unknowns: Whether this clinic's patient record already lists activity rows for a chosen period.
How often a care activity is stored with no activity code.
Whether a care-activity report may be filed without a second clinician's countersignature.
research_questions: What share of care activities on this ward is entered as a coded row at the time of care?

already_counted.description: Reading the draft against the marked notes and the activity selection.

incremental.description: Monthly sample of filed reports for a line the marked notes do not support.
A document administrator updates report headings when the clinic changes activity codes.

approvals.approved_version: Care-activity report for this period, as the clinical nurse specialist confirmed it against the marked notes and the activity selection. A later change voids the confirmation. This file is not a prescription.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only placing the selected activity rows, the first narrative, and filing the confirmed text lose time. Asking the ward, reading the notes, choosing the activities and the check stay at full time. When coded rows are missing she writes those reports herself, so a thin week saves a few hours. One hour per 100 baseline hours is the monthly sample. The published note-time study is not applied here.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still asks the ward, reads the notes and chooses which activities the reports document. A confirmed report keeps that choice. She does not gain a right to prescribe or to file a line she did not check.
reach: The ward nurse enters the activity code when the care is given, and reads the confirmed report rather than the draft.
The medical records specialist retains the filed report for the dossier period and does not treat a blank draft as a record.
skills_to_grow: Leave the narrative blank when the marked notes do not support a line.
Mark the activity selection before the shell is filled, including short stays.
Reject a sentence that names an activity she did not choose.
role.ambitious_version: Each period she chooses has a confirmed report whose lines cite the rows and the notes she marked. She still asks, reads and decides. Nothing is filed that she did not check.
